DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 91 s. 2022 SEP 14 2022 ATTY. FRANCES MAE CHERRYL K. ONTALAN Director IV, Legal Service Department of Health 3rd Flr., Building 12, San Lorenzo Compound, Rizal Avenue, Sta. Cruz, Manila Dear Atty. Ontalan: This has reference to your letter dated 21 June 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on whether the ordinances or issuances from local government units providing exemption from vaccination which are not contained in IA TF Resolutions, valid and binding upon the Department of Education. Per your representation, the query is one of the several questions proffered in the DepEd letter dated 22 March 2022 addressed to the COVID19 Inter-Agency Task Force (IATF) regarding the implementation of IA TF Resolution Nos. 148-B and 149 Series of 2021. Foremost, please be apprised that this Department, in its previous legal opinions, has been consistent that inasmuch as the ordinance has undergone the procedural process for its enactment pursuant to the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), the same is considered valid unless declared otherwise by courts. Accordingly, this Department is bereft of authority to rule on the legality of the subject ordinance in question as this is within the jurisdiction of the regular courts. Thus, any issues concerning the validity of an ordinance shall be threshed out before the éroper court. Notwithstanding, for purposes of academic discussion, it is settled that local ordinances are binding within their territorial limits of the local government unit and must have statutory or constitutional authority to stand on. 1 An ordinance must not contravene the Constitution and any statute, and must be general in application and consistent with public policy.2 In this regard, this Department would like to emphasize that while the local government units (LGUs) enjoy local autonomy and are empowered to issue the necessary orders 1 City of Manila V. Judge Laguio, G.R. NO. 118127, 12 April 2005 2 Solicitor General V. Metropolitan Manila Authority, 204 SCRA 837 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

within their jurisdiction pursuant to the to the general welfare clause provided under the LGC, however, it must, at all times, make sure that such orders are in harmony and compliant with existing laws and policies of the national task force and applicable protocols. Hence, all orders and issuances passed by LGUs must adhere to the directives of the national government, and if said orders or issuances were passed prior to the adoption of said policies, the LGU concerned should take the initiative in modifying/amending its directive to conform thereto. In view of the foregoing, the concerned LGU and its sanggunian should be encouraged to modify/amend issuances or ordinances to correspond with existing laws, policies of the national government, and guidelines of the IATF, considering that under the Memorandum dated 18 March 2020 issued by the Office of the Executive Secretary, directs all heads of departments, agencies, and instrumentalities of the government, including LGUs, among others, to adopt, coordinate, and implement guidelines which the IATF may issue on the COVID-19 situation, consistent with the respective agency mandates and relevant laws, rules, and regulations. Be that as it may, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: Undersec ry for Local Government OSEC/BCA/LLLS-LRALLD/1asm/rjki/clp copy furnish: DIR. MARIA LOURDES L. AGUSTIN Regional Director, DILG-NCR Annex Building, Sugar Center Compound North Ave., Diliman, Quezon City Page 2 of 2
